speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing a psychiatric condition alongside a new movement disorder; to begin our assessment, can you describe exactly what movements you are noticing and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news regarding your psychiatric improvement. Given the risperidone you started two months ago, I need to know if your new movement disorder involves involuntary muscle contractions, stiffness, tremors, or a feeling of restlessness. Please describe exactly what you are seeing or feeling.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you are describing—specifically the inability to remain still, fidgeting, and repetitive leg movements—are classic signs of acute dystonia or akathisia. Given your history of starting risperidone recently, this is a high probability. Were these symptoms present immediately after taking your first dose, or did they develop gradually over the past few weeks? REQUEST TEST: Risperidone_Dosage_and_Compliance.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the details; the normal readings don't change our clinical picture. Since your symptoms of restlessness and fidgeting are highly suggestive of drug-induced akathisia from the risperidone, are you experiencing any pain or muscle spasms in your neck or jaw, or any tremors in your hands? REQUEST TEST: Risperidone_Blood_Level.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Akathisia (secondary to Risperidone therapy).
